message:
fix(update): the updater was asking windowless children to close, which cannot work

GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent takes a process GROUP id, not a pid. It succeeds only if
that pid is a group leader AND shares our console, and the supervisor starts its
children with neither. So for GNLinkStream and GNLinkCapture the request had no
success case at all -- and PrepareForSwap abandons on the first failure, which is
why an update could not run while either was alive. The field log says it
plainly: "could not ask pid 9132 to stop".

Why no test caught it: request_process_stop has one caller in the product and
none anywhere in the suite. All eleven assignments of requestStop are lambdas,
including the ones named as failure cases, so the branch that actually failed had
never executed. update_effects_test.cpp:8 says so in as many words. Linking a
file in CMake is not evidence that anything calls it.

The fix routes a windowless process to its supervisor instead of asking it
directly, the way closing an application leaves it to close its own children.
Ownership is verified, never assumed: the parent must be one of the targets, have
a window, and have started first. Miss any of the three and the process is asked
directly rather than quietly adopted.

Quiesce now waits on the list PrepareForSwap worked from. Re-enumerating meant
waiting for whatever had started in between, and silently not waiting for
something already asked and on its way out. ACCESS_DENIED from OpenProcess is no
longer read as "it exited" -- that is "cannot tell", and treating it as an exit is
how an update proceeds over a process still holding the files. And "outlived its
parent" is now a different message from "did not exit"; only the first means the
supervisor contract broke.

The counterexample runs real processes through the real functions: a windowed
parent (created, never shown) and a windowless, consoleless child. It asserts the
old routing still fails with the field's own message, and that the new one
succeeds. Removing the routing turns it red with "could not ask pid N to stop".

Also the regression the verifier asked for: GNLinkUpdater.exe was in payloadNames
and nothing had ever watched a swap replace it -- "the updater can be updated"
rested on a name being in a vector, which is the same shape as the mistake that
left it out. It is now staged and swapped for real, with the opposite direction
asserted too (an updater running from inside the install directory is refused).
The assembly fixture was driving production's flow with a different payload list;
it uses product_payload_names() now.

64 suites, 1811 checks, no failures -- with the console session attached. That
also closes #497: the four capture and encoder suites, and udp_control_e2e, pass
when re-run on the console with the same binaries.
